question: Do disagreement-only training and early consensus conditioning improve reliable selection?
scope_D: 2114 questions with at least two distinct valid parsed answers, computed from inputs only
preprocessing: shared input and six-feature standardization fitted to all training inputs only, identical for both scopes
injection: 6-to-128 bias-free linear projection, zero initialized; Early after encoder before FFN/attention; Late after interaction/norm before unchanged head
P: only valid_parse active; five consensus dimensions zero after standardization
C: all six prior parse/consensus features active
loss: all four candidate BCE on each sampled question, no weighting
sampling: cyclic shuffled pool, leftover indices retained across budget epochs; P/C and Early/Late within scope share exact draws
checkpoint: last budget only, no early stopping or validation selection
inference: all predictors: one valid numeric answer group -> first valid candidate, no model; otherwise neural scoring then invalid-answer exclusion
primary_contrasts: D-All averaged over feature and position
Early-Late at C averaged over scope
(Early-Late at C)-(Early-Late at P), averaged over scope
(Early-Late at D)-(Early-Late at All), averaged over feature
secondary_contrasts: all simple effects and full 2x2x2 interactions, wrong-consensus and other prespecified diagnostic groups
ensembles: one equal mean sigmoid five-seed predictor per cell, secondary

bootstrap.scope: descriptive conditional on fitted models and repeated validation development, no multiplicity correction

selection: no winner selected; every predeclared cell retained
